_comment: Western-flank cavalry charge into a troop standing just south of the impassable hill. The flank angle is deliberate, learned by dumping three failed stagings: a charge from dead behind overshoots NORTH onto the flee lane and physically walls it, a rear cavalry pursuer that stays in contact herds and grinds the mob before any detour shows, and archer fire pins the mob prone into a crawl. Under the regiment-formula opening blow this matchup used to break on contact, overshoot EAST, and send the rout north around the hill -- PathField.next_step_fleeing() at the unit's own clearance margin. Opening melee is per-soldier now: a deep 80-horse column's facing-front sits a mounted rank-pitch past the defender and lands no opening wounds, while a shallow troop that actually hits stays in contact and herds instead of punching through. This clip therefore no longer claims the instant-rout detour; that restage (shallow enough to wound, still overshooting off the flee lane) is a follow-up. This scenario does NOT demonstrate the separate 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' behavior -- the hill is a single free-standing obstacle nowhere near a field edge, so terrain alone can never fully enclose a unit here; that behavior is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing, which stages a real sealed ring directly. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. The pursuer's own formation progressively deforms during a long gallop chase -- a known, separately tracked sim/calibration question -- so mid-gallop samples of the pursuer's cosmetics are deliberately not part of this clip's declared checks.
